05-rig.jpg.contentAnchor: Your scoreboard program is built — this part keeps it safe before the Rally. You are going to save a copy into your Google Drive, the same way as last lesson: three steps, about a minute. In a real rally every car is checked in before the race — your RIG is your scoreboard program, and this is its check-in. When the file is in your Drive, press Check my Drive below, and the website will look to make sure it is really there. Then even if a cable is pulled out mid-Rally, your work is safe.

06-rally.jpg.name: 06-rally.jpg
06-rally.jpg.textSnippet: This is the Reaction Rally — the speed test your scoreboard was built for. You play in your pair, but every pupil plays for herself: two goes each, and your scores go in under your own name. The game:
06-rally.jpg.contentAnchor: This is the Reaction Rally — the speed test your scoreboard was built for. You play in your pair, but every pupil plays for herself: two goes each, and your scores go in under your own name. The game: while the timer on this screen runs, press button A as fast as you can. Your scoreboard counts every press — the number in the box is your score. You are also secretly on a team. The website has mixed the class into four hidden teams, and every score you send in is added to your team's total. Nobody finds out who is on which team until your teacher reveals them on the big screen at the end of the lesson. One of you plays while the other one referees, then you swap jobs. The referee's job is to keep the test fair — the rules below say how.
